scope: P14 backend integration, PostgreSQL migrations and existing backend regressions. Browser verification is recorded separately.

observations: The legacy V001 upgrade test expected migrations only through V015 while V016 had actually migrated.
The operator attachment test expected a selection conflict; the empty-attachment requirement is rejected as structural validation (400 VALIDATION_FAILED), with no message persisted.

Two concurrent first CSRF-token reads preceded the concurrent issuance requests and one request returned 403. The test now initializes one valid session token before the request barrier while retaining two concurrent database mutations. No production security control was weakened.

package.note: Packaging skipped tests after the successful 42-test targeted run. The subsequent global verify executed all 221 tests and repackaged the artifact.

boundaries: Verification did not load .env.local; the public verify command disables inherited real Stripe settings and background payment/refund workers. Test suites provide their own isolated controlled settings.
Sensitive integration paths use PostgreSQL, actual local S3 and SMTP/Mailpit transports where applicable. Controlled Stripe HTTP transports are distinct from external Stripe services.

Only test names, result counts, timings, artifact metadata and non-sensitive validation history were extracted. No JUnit system properties, logs, credentials, private productions or payloads are included.
This record does not claim browser, external Stripe, CI, deployment or production validation.

previousGlobals.exitCodeObservation: The tool call was interrupted before returning a session identifier; the shell exit code was not collected. The completed Maven log reports BUILD SUCCESS and agrees with all current JUnit reports.
previousGlobals.note: Successful backend verification before the subsequently observed data-event ordering defect and the causal timestamp correction.

previousPackage.note: Packaging skipped test execution after the successful targeted run. The following global verify executed all 219 tests and repackaged the artifact.

causalCorrection.observedDefect: A browser run returned CANCELLED before REQUESTED. Whether timestamp equality or clock movement caused that occurrence is unknown because the isolated database had already been cleaned.
causalCorrection.implementation: Data lifecycle events are read in REQUESTED then CANCELLED order. New account/support actions use one PostgreSQL timestamp strictly after stored parent and child predecessors, including future predecessors.
causalCorrection.preservation: No V016 modification or V017 migration. Historical timestamps and immutable rows are preserved; tests insert explicit synthetic historical rows without disabling guards.
